intended_object: For an open immersion j : U → Y, the canonical morphism (in fact an isomorphism) of sheaves of rings 𝒪_U → 𝒪_Y|_U. Here 𝒪_Y|_U is the pushforward of 𝒪_Y along the functor W ↦ j(W) on opens, and on sections over W the map is the inverse of the canonical iso 𝒪_Y(j(W)) ≅ 𝒪_U(W). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in defining `restrictFunctor j` as a pushforward of sheaves of modules.
explanation:
The body is a word-for-word copy of the ring-sheaf morphism that Mathlib builds inline inside `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor` in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean`. Mathlib builds the same morphism inline a second time, in `Tilde.lean`.

The definition does this:
- It builds the natural transformation α : U.presheaf ⟶ j.opensFunctor.op ⋙ Y.presheaf, whose components are `(j.appIso W).inv`.
- It whiskers α with the forgetful functor CommRingCat ⥤ RingCat.
- It wraps the result as a morphism of sheaves into the pushforward of Y.ringCatSheaf along `j.opensFunctor`.

That is exactly the canonical identification 𝒪_U(W) ≅ 𝒪_Y(j(W)), read in the direction 𝒪_U → 𝒪_Y|_U, which is what the docstring says.

The generality is the natural one. The construction needs the hypothesis `IsOpenImmersion`: `appIso` and `opensFunctor` only exist for open immersions, and the definition does not ask for anything more.

Mathlib has no standalone named declaration for this morphism; it appears only inside other definitions. So there is no `mathlib_counterpart` to cite, and nothing of which this definition is a narrower version.
